subject.title: [Feature]: cron add: support custom job IDs via --id

question: Should cron's public create contract accept caller-supplied job IDs, and if so what validation and scope should apply across CLI, Gateway API, docs, tests, and the agent cron tool?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this changes a public identifier surface and the repository policy treats CLI/Gateway contract additions as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Adopt custom IDs across create surfaces
options.body: Add an optional validated ID to CLI, Gateway protocol, service creation, docs, and focused tests, with duplicate rejection and UUID generation unchanged when omitted.

options.title: Limit the feature to CLI and Gateway
options.body: Expose custom IDs only for operator-facing create calls and explicitly leave the agent cron tool unchanged until a separate model-facing contract decision is made.

options.title: Decline custom create IDs
options.body: Keep UUID-only creation and improve listing, display, or docs instead, accepting that scripts must continue referencing generated IDs.

recommendation.title: Adopt custom IDs across create surfaces
recommendation.body: Add an optional validated ID to CLI, Gateway protocol, service creation, docs, and focused tests, with duplicate rejection and UUID generation unchanged when omitted.

likelyOwner.reason: The scheduler and cron create ergonomics history makes this the best available owner for the public cron contract decision.
